name: The Stolen Flour
initial_prompt: Mara asks you to recover the flour Toma took. Find out what happened and decide what to do.
storyteller_summary: Mara promised Toma a sack of flour for repairing the mill. He finished the work. A flood spoiled the other village stores, so Mara withheld payment to ration the sack among several households. Toma took it anyway; his household also needs food. Both acknowledge the debt. Neither has replacement food in hand.

gm.opening: The Adventurer and Mara are outside Toma's home's barred front door. Toma is in the front room; the flour is stored in a separate rear room. Mara wants it returned without anyone being hurt. The rear window is found by going around and examining the back of the house.
gm.dispute: The work and promised payment are real. Mara's emergency does not erase Toma's claim; his claim does not feed the other households. What happens depends on the characters' decisions.

groups.name: charcoal hut
groups.description: Mara and the Adventurer outside Toma's home; Toma in the front room, his flour stored in the rear room.

gm.grouping: One group covers the hut and its immediate surroundings. Voices carry through the boards, but walls and distance still constrain sight and access.

locations.name: charcoal hut
locations.description: Toma's small timber home, converted from a charcoal-burner's hut. Its front door is barred; bushes grow behind the house.

gm.interior: Toma is in the front room with his work axe within reach. The tied flour sack is in a separate rear room. The partition blocks his view of it, but he can hear movement on the wooden floor. Carrying the sack takes both arms.
gm.exterior: Mara and the Adventurer start outside the barred front door. Going around and examining the rear reveals a window behind bushes with an unlatched shutter. Finding it needs no roll. The window admits a person and the sack, passed through separately. Moving around the house is local movement.
gm.stealth: Climbing into the rear room and moving the sack unnoticed requires a DEX save for the stealth attempt: Toma cannot see into the room but can hear noise. Explain the consequence before the actual recorded roll. Success allows the feasible attempt to proceed unnoticed; failure brings Toma to investigate and confront the intruder. Being caught sneaking into his home gives him reason to distrust the player, making later discussion harder. Combat is possible, not automatic. Conversation at the front can occupy him but does not eliminate the noise risk.

npcs.name: Mara
npcs.description: The village storekeeper, outside the hut, worried about the households relying on her.
npcs.background: I promised Toma a sack of flour for repairing the mill. He completed the work. A flood spoiled the other village stores, so I withheld his payment to ration this sack among several households. He took it anyway. His household also needs food. I know I owe him; I have no replacement food in hand.
npcs.motive: Recover the flour for the village households without anyone being hurt.
npcs.ambition: Keep the households depending on me fed. I feel responsible for them and defensive about withholding Toma's payment.

gm.knowledge: Mara acknowledges the completed work and the promised payment. She has no authority to promise another household's resources.

npcs.name: Toma
npcs.description: A healthy mill worker in worn clothes, in the front room of his home, with a wood axe within reach.
npcs.background: Mara promised me this sack of flour as wages for repairing the mill. I finished the work. After a flood ruined the other village stores she withheld payment to ration it among households. I took my wages home and stored the flour in my rear room. I am in the front room: the partition blocks my view of the flour, but I can hear movement behind it. My household is also short of food. I am proud of my work, resent being treated as a thief, and distrust another promise from Mara. I have no replacement food in hand.
npcs.motive: Keep my earned food for my household without violence.
npcs.ambition: Have my work respected and my household fed.

beliefs: The sack is my earned payment.
The flood was not my fault.
Mara has already broken her promise.
gm.position: Toma is in his front room, with no direct view into the rear room where the flour is stored. Noise can alert him. He is healthy and can confront an intruder; carrying the sack occupies both arms.

item_types.name: flour sack
item_types.description: One full sack of flour. Carrying it occupies both arms. Two half flour sacks can be combined into this type.

item_types.name: half flour sack
item_types.description: Half the contents of one full flour sack. Splitting a full sack produces two items of this type; combining those halves restores one full sack.

items.name: flour sack
items.description: A tied, bulky sack of flour. Carrying it occupies both arms.

gm.state: Stored in Toma's rear room, out of sight from his front room, accessible through the rear window. Moving it quietly is the stealth challenge. Toma considers it his earned payment. Ordinary careful handling preserves the flour; a struggle or a blade can spill it.

items.name: wood axe
items.description: Toma's work axe, within his reach inside the hut.

gm.state: An ordinary wood axe, d6 damage. It is beside Toma, not unattended outside.
